messages:
Sara Patel: heads-up — I ran into a fairness regression while comparing latest kernel-selection ops with the older branch. multi-tenant workloads show one tenant saturating batches and others starving during sustained bursts. wondering if we should standardize a new harness that mixes replay traffic + synthetic microbursts so comparisons are apples-to-apples :thinking_face:
Mike Chen: can you paste the perf diff? last time the kernel tweak increased single-step kernel latency and that made batching decisions back off in the scheduler (resulting in larger per-tenant skew).
Sara Patel: sure, rough numbers from a short run: 
```
old: gpu_kern_time_ms=2.34 avg, kv_lookup_ms=0.41
new: gpu_kern_time_ms=3.11 avg, kv_lookup_ms=0.43
end-to-end p95 increased ~14% for mixed tenants
```
Anika Rao: ugh. two noisy axes: (1) kv-cache warmup/thrashing, (2) continuous batching heuristics (batchcap/max-delay) + kernel throughput profile. we need a harness that controls both. propose: replay baseline (real traces) -> deterministic synthetic overlay (microbursts of X req/s targeting tenant set) -> configurable kv-warmup period.
Devon Li: agree. also lock batchcap and max-delay across runs so scheduler decisions don't vary from run to run. otherwise changes in arrival timing make the comparison meaningless.
Oscar Kim: for metrics, capture per-tenant tokens/s, batch size distribution, evicted-kv-count, and kernel execution histogram (ms). we should compute an unfairness metric: (p90 throughput of top-3 tenants) / (median tenant p90). want that as a single number per run.
Sara Patel: good metric. i can add that to the harness output. thinking of CLI like:
```
./tools/replay_harness \
  --replay=traces/multi_tenant_jan.replay \
  --overlay=synthetic/microburst-8x.json \
  --batchcap=64 \
  --max-delay-ms=20 \
  --kv-warmup-secs=120 \
  --collect-profile=/tmp/run123.perf
```
Anika Rao: add also a short prefix-length sweep option to test KV hit-rate sensitivity. kv-warmup-secs=120 should be the default but run with 0/30/120 to see delta. include a step to flush kv between runs: `curl -XPOST $SERVE/_admin/kv/flush`
Mike Chen: to reproduce the kernel regression, pin the runtime to commit abc123 vs def456 and run the same harness with identical seeds. i saw this in a micro-bench: `gpu memcpy: 0.8ms -> 1.4ms` which shifted the batching window. small kernel increases -> bigger queuing impact.
replay-bot: run 2026-03-15T22:13:04Z complete: 8 tenants, 5m steady + 30s microbursts. results: link: https://internal.redwood/devtools/runs/6732 (artifact: profile.tar.gz) :white_check_mark:
Oscar Kim: can someone pull the trace and the profile.tar.gz? i'd like to run the unfairness calc and a flamegraph. also we should add a per-tenant latency CDF overlay plot in the dashboard.
Sara Patel: assigning: Oscar, can you run the suite on a dedicated node (no autoscaling) and attach perf + nvprof output? set `--isolated-node=true`. if it shows the same skew we'll dig into kernel scheduling.
Oscar Kim: on it. i'll run today and post summary here. will do runs for batchcap in [32,64,128] and max-delay-ms in [10,20,50]. also try kv-warmup 0/30/120.
Devon Li: please capture per-batch tenant composition (which tenant ids are batched together) — that will show whether the scheduler is favoring recent arrivals.
Anika Rao: small note — when comparing kernel variants, normalize by sample sequence length distribution. different seq-lens change kernel phasing (attention cost). include `--seq-dist=control.json` to fix that.
Mike Chen: perf hint: collect `gpu_active_ms`, `kernel_launch_wait_ms`, and `kv_lookup_miss_rate`. simple grep-able stdout lines make CI parsing easier.
Sara Patel: thanks all. Oscar — ping me when you post the run. if we confirm regression i'll open a perf-incident and assign kernel team. :eyes:
Oscar Kim: will do. ETA ~3h.
replay-bot: note: remember to annotate runs with `branch` and `commit` fields so we can group results by kernel selection policy.
Sara Patel: added test checklist to the harness README and the /runs metadata template. thanks :thumbsup:
Oscar Kim: first run finished, uploading artifacts now — will post link when available.
Sara Patel: perfect — once we have profiles we'll decide rollback vs tweak kernel heuristics.
Oscar Kim: upload complete: https://internal.redwood/devtools/runs/6799 (includes flamegraphs and per-tenant batch histograms). initial glance: batch composition skew correlates with increased kernel tail. leaving full analysis for the next post. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
